record.original_question: Does the Banach space B(ℓ₂) of all bounded linear operators from ℓ₂ to itself, equipped with the operator norm, have the approximation property? Also, does the Banach space of all bounded analytic functions on the open unit disk, equipped with the supremum norm, have the approximation property?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Banach space $X$ is said to have the approximation property if for every compact subset $K \subset X$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a bounded finite-rank linear operator $T : X \to X$ such that $\|Tx - x\| < \varepsilon$ for all $x \in K$.

Consider the following two Banach spaces:

(a) $B(\ell_2)$, the space of all bounded linear operators from $\ell_2$ into itself, equipped with the operator norm $\|T\| = \sup_{\|x\|_{\ell_2} \le 1} \|Tx\|_{\ell_2}$.

(b) $H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$, the space of all bounded analytic functions $f$ on the open unit disk $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$, equipped with the supremum norm $\|f\|_\infty = \sup_{z \in \mathbb{D}} |f(z)|$.

Determine whether each of these Banach spaces has the approximation property.
artifact.status_search_result: The question for $B(\ell_2)$ was resolved by A. Szankowski (1981), who proved that $B(\ell_2)$ fails the approximation property. The question of whether $H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$ has the approximation property is a well-known long-standing open problem in Banach space theory, still unresolved as of recent literature.

status_evidence.snippet: Concerns approximation property questions related to H∞ spaces; the AP for H∞ of the disk is referenced as an outstanding open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The approximation property for H^∞(D) remains an open problem.

status_evidence.snippet: Background on H^∞ and Hardy spaces on the disk.
status_evidence.claim: H^∞(D) is the Banach space of bounded analytic functions on the unit disk with the supremum norm.
